observations: The first paragraph now defines an isotherm using pressure, volume and fixed temperature, then identifies the same pure substance and total mass in Figure 55.
The next paragraph explains the flat part as liquid and vapor both being present. The reader no longer has to decode liquid-vapor coexistence segment before knowing what to inspect.
Below-critical scope is explicit both for the shortening flat parts and for the condensation-volume comparison. The opening does not extend those coexistence endpoints above the critical temperature.
The unchanged equal-pressure-at-each-temperature and different-pressure-between-temperatures sentences remain intact, as does the rejection of constant-pressure heating.

observations: The saturated-liquid branch and saturated-vapor pressure curve are named separately, with their respective critical-volume and critical-pressure endpoints. The old They mean the endpoint construction is gone.

A separate short paragraph states that these are not limits for every state; pressure can exceed critical pressure and liquid volume depends on conditions. Fixed mass remains explicit for the liquid branch.
The compression passage explains one fluid becoming denser and more liquid-like without splitting into separate liquid and vapor regions. The unconditionally and finite interval wording is gone.
The absent two-phase volume range is connected to the already explained flat coexistence segment. Continuous density change is still distinguished from strong changes in other physical properties.
The earlier critical-temperature, critical-density and fixed-mass sentences, the pressure examples and all mathematical fragments are unchanged.
findingResolutions.readabilityJudgment: The revised clauses name each quantity and visible phase distinction directly. They resolve the original abstract wording without discarding the required caveats.
findingResolutions.affectedScienceJudgment: No universal pressure or volume maximum was introduced. Critical-temperature compression remains continuous and single-phase, not a blanket ordinary-liquid claim; no claim that all properties vary gently was introduced.
